front_blocks.md: Define **carboxylic acid**.

back_blocks.md: A **carboxylic acid** is an organic compound containing the **carboxyl** (-COOH) functional group. The general formula is C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+1</sub>COOH.

cards.back_md: A **carboxylic acid** is an organic compound containing the **carboxyl** (-COOH) functional group. The general formula is C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+1</sub>COOH.

front_blocks.md: How are carboxylic acids named?

back_blocks.md: Carboxylic acids are named using the pattern **alkan + oic acid**. For example, the two-carbon acid is called **ethanoic acid**.

cards.back_md: Carboxylic acids are named using the pattern **alkan + oic acid**. For example, the two-carbon acid is called **ethanoic acid**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Vinegar is a dilute aqueous solution of ethanoic acid.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Vinegar** contains about 5% **ethanoic acid** by volume dissolved in water. Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid with the formula CH<sub>3</sub>COOH.

front_blocks.md: The carbon atom in the **..........** functional group is counted as part of the carbon chain, so CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COOH has **..........** carbon atoms and is called butanoic acid.

back_blocks.md: The carbon atom in the **-COOH** functional group is counted as part of the carbon chain, so CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COOH has **four** carbon atoms and is called butanoic acid.

front_blocks.md: What is the **carboxyl group**?

back_blocks.md: The **carboxyl group** is the -COOH functional group found in all **carboxylic acids**. It consists of a carbonyl (C=O) and a hydroxyl (-OH) group bonded to the same carbon atom.

cards.back_md: The **carboxyl group** is the -COOH functional group found in all **carboxylic acids**. It consists of a carbonyl (C=O) and a hydroxyl (-OH) group bonded to the same carbon atom.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The general formula of a carboxylic acid can be written as RCOOH.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
RCOOH is a shorthand for the general formula of a **carboxylic acid**, where **R** represents the varying **hydrocarbon** chain attached to the -COOH group.

front_blocks.md: What is the formula of ethanoic acid?

back_blocks.md: The formula of **ethanoic acid** is CH<sub>3</sub>COOH. It is the second member of the carboxylic acid series and is found in **vinegar**.

cards.front_md: What is the formula of ethanoic acid?

front_blocks.md: What two types of substance do carboxylic acids react with?

back_blocks.md: Carboxylic acids react with **metals** and **carbonates**. This behaviour is typical of acids in general.

cards.front_md: What two types of substance do carboxylic acids react with?
cards.back_md: Carboxylic acids react with **metals** and **carbonates**. This behaviour is typical of acids in general.

front_blocks.md: When a carboxylic acid reacts with a metal, it produces a **..........** and **..........** gas.

back_blocks.md: When a carboxylic acid reacts with a metal, it produces a **salt** and **hydrogen** gas.

cards.front_md: When a carboxylic acid reacts with a metal, it produces a **..........** and **..........** gas.
cards.back_md: When a carboxylic acid reacts with a metal, it produces a **salt** and **hydrogen** gas.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Salts formed from carboxylic acids end in the suffix -anoate.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The salts of **carboxylic acids** all end in **-anoate**. For example, ethanoic acid forms salts called **ethanoates**.

front_blocks.md: When a carboxylic acid reacts with a carbonate, the products are a salt, **..........** and **..........** gas.

back_blocks.md: When a carboxylic acid reacts with a carbonate, the products are a salt, **water** and **carbon dioxide** gas.

cards.back_md: When a carboxylic acid reacts with a carbonate, the products are a salt, **water** and **carbon dioxide** gas.

front_blocks.md: What is the name of the salt formed when ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium?

back_blocks.md: The salt formed is **magnesium ethanoate**. This follows the naming rule that salts from carboxylic acids end in **-anoate**.

cards.front_md: What is the name of the salt formed when ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium?
cards.back_md: The salt formed is **magnesium ethanoate**. This follows the naming rule that salts from carboxylic acids end in **-anoate**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Butanoic acid reacts with potassium carbonate to form potassium butanoate.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Butanoic acid** reacts with **potassium carbonate** to form **potassium butanoate**, water and carbon dioxide. This is a typical reaction of a carboxylic acid with a carbonate.

front_blocks.md: What does the suffix **-anoate** tell you about a compound?

back_blocks.md: **-anoate** tells you the compound is a salt formed from a **carboxylic acid**. For example, magnesium ethanoate is the salt of **ethanoic acid**.
